background: DNB is Norway's largest bank, part-owned by the Norwegian state, funded by Norwegian deposits and covered bonds and lending to Norwegian households and companies, with a large shipping and energy book.
synthesis: Two of the three main agencies rate the bank, at AA on average and the weakest of them at AA-, both on a stable outlook, with a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 27 Sep 2023 the latest move. Capital is strong against EU and Nordic peers, with CET1 of 17.4% and leverage of 6.3% both above the peer medians, though CET1 has fallen 1.6 points since 30 Jun 2024. Liquidity is the weak side: LCR of 136% and NSFR of 116% are both in the bottom quarter against the peer medians. Nothing has been flagged in the last 90 days. A highly rated name whose liquidity ratios sit lower than the ratings might suggest.
